<u>Fish</u> - The species of fish that were identified from the Sarpy drainage are listed in Appendix F. Of seventeen species identified, only three occured in the immediate vicinity of the lease. These were the Lake Chub (<u>Couesius plumbeus</u>), Fathead Minnow (<u>Pimephales promelas</u>), White Sucker (<u>Catostomus commersoni</u>). The remainder of the fish species collected were found north of the leases in lower Sarpy Creek, with the majority of these being taken near its confluence with the Yellowstone River. The Sauger was the only Montana game fish collected from Sarpy Creek. Most of the fish move downstream away from the project area as streams stagnate in summer (Dames and Moore 1975).
Endangered and Threatened Species
Four species, three birds and one mammal, possibly occurring in the region of the Project Area have been placed under the Federal Protection offered by the Endangered Species Act of 1973.
The peregrine falcon (<u>Falco peregrinus</u>) is listed as endangered (Office of Endangered Species and International Activities, 1974) because cumulative effects of chlorinated pesticides and their metabolites obtained from prey have caused increased adult mortality and a reduced production of young. Habitat destruction and removal of birds from the wild for falconry have been listed as factors (Office of Endangered Species and International Activities, 1973). Breeding and winter records of this species in Montana have been confirmed (Environment and Information Division, 1974). The peregrine falcon has not been observed in the Project Area, and it is unlikely that it would be present except as a migrant.
